tldr: Sharp population variance completion need not admit precise calibration from one experimental record per stratum. The focal object is the largest true normalized design variance compatible with the complete average law of treatment and control success counts. Pure table laws identify their true variance, but mixing them produces a nonlinear envelope, and a sixteen-unit collision separates the envelope from all observable quadratic moments. The central open question seeks an evaluated constant-factor estimation frontier for every number and size of binary half-randomized strata, with a total attaining estimator and an original-record converse. An established attaining risk bound permits honest one-sided padding and conservative finite-cohort ATE inference under the maintained finite-sample variance floor of this note, while a matching-based interval remains valid outside shrinking-calibration regimes.
gap: \cite{YuZhuLiu2025} motivates marginal-sharp variance calibration, and \cite{HarshawMiddletonSavje2026} optimizes estimable quadratic bounds and their precision. Neither solves feasible estimation of the full-count-law variance envelope. The closest risk duality applies to affine or separable targets; this target violates that premise.
